discovery: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background using pulsar timing arrays

nominees.name: Michael Kramer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany

motivation: In 2023 the pulsar timing array collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA/InPTA, PPTA) reported consistent evidence for a stochastic gravitational-wave background at nanohertz frequencies. The key evidence was the Hellings-Downs angular correlation across arrays of millisecond pulsars, the long-predicted signature of gravitational waves. The result opens a new window, many orders of magnitude below LIGO frequencies, onto supermassive black-hole binaries and possibly early-universe sources such as first-order phase transitions, cosmic strings or inflationary relics. It took two decades of precise timing, instrument development and statistical method-building to reach it. McLaughlin co-founded and led NANOGrav. Kramer built up the European effort and its high-precision timing, through the double pulsar and the EPTA. Manchester pioneered Parkes pulsar timing and the PPTA. Together they turned galactic clocks into a detector the size of the Galaxy, which makes early-universe physics testable.
